passages.text: So the king and Haman went to dine with Esther the queen, and as they drank their wine on that second day, the king asked once more, “Queen Esther, what is your petition? It will be given to you. What is your request? Even up to half the kingdom, it will be fulfilled.”
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes was the ruler of Persia.
Haman was his high official.
Esther was the queen.
The king and Haman went to eat with Queen Esther.
They drank wine together.
This was the second day of the banquet.
The king spoke to Esther again.
He said, “Queen Esther, what do you ask for?”
He said, “It will be given to you.”
He said, “What is your request?”
He said, “Even if you ask for half the kingdom, it will be done.”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֤א הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ וְהָמָ֔ן לִשְׁתּ֖וֹת עִם־ אֶסְתֵּ֥ר הַמַּלְכָּֽה׃ וַיֹּאמֶר֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ לְאֶסְתֵּ֜ר גַּ֣ם בַּיּ֤וֹם הַשֵּׁנִי֙ בְּמִשְׁתֵּ֣ה הַיַּ֔יִן מַה־ שְּׁאֵלָתֵ֛ךְ אֶסְתֵּ֥ר הַמַּלְכָּ֖ה וְתִנָּ֣תֵֽן לָ֑ךְ וּמַה־ בַּקָּשָׁתֵ֛ךְ עַד־ חֲצִ֥י הַמַּלְכ֖וּת וְתֵעָֽשׂ׃

passages.text: Queen Esther replied, “If I have found favor in your sight, O king, and if it pleases the king, grant me my life as my petition, and the lives of my people as my request.
passages.sermon:
Queen Esther spoke to King Xerxes.
She answered the king’s question.
She said, “If I have found favor in your eyes, O king, and if it pleases you, grant me my life.
This is my petition.
Grant the lives of my people.
This is my request.”
passages.original: וַתַּ֨עַן אֶסְתֵּ֤ר הַמַּלְכָּה֙ וַתֹּאמַ֔ר אִם־ מָצָ֨אתִי חֵ֤ן בְּעֵינֶ֙יךָ֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְאִם־ עַל־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ ט֑וֹב תִּנָּֽתֶן־ לִ֤י נַפְשִׁי֙ בִּשְׁאֵ֣לָתִ֔י וְעַמִּ֖י בְּבַקָּשָׁתִֽי׃

passages.text: For my people and I have been sold out to destruction, death, and annihilation. If we had merely been sold as menservants and maidservants, I would have remained silent, because no such distress would justify burdening the king.”
passages.sermon:
Esther was a Jewish queen of Persia.
She spoke to King Xerxes.
Esther said, “My people and I have been sold.
We have been sold to be destroyed.
We have been sold to be killed.
We have been sold to be wiped out.
If we had only been sold as slaves,
If we had only been sold as male and female servants,
I would have kept silent.
I would not have troubled the king.
Such trouble would not be worth disturbing the king.”
passages.original: כִּ֤י נִמְכַּ֙רְנוּ֙ אֲנִ֣י וְעַמִּ֔י לְהַשְׁמִ֖יד לַהֲר֣וֹג וּלְאַבֵּ֑ד וְ֠אִלּוּ לַעֲבָדִ֨ים וְלִשְׁפָח֤וֹת נִמְכַּ֙רְנוּ֙ הֶחֱרַ֔שְׁתִּי כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין הַצָּ֛ר שֹׁוֶ֖ה בְּנֵ֥זֶק הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס

passages.text: Then King Xerxes spoke up and asked Queen Esther, “Who is this, and where is the one who would devise such a scheme?”
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes was the ruler of Persia.
Queen Esther was his wife.
King Xerxes spoke to Queen Esther.
He asked her a question.
He said, “Who is this person?”
He also said, “Where is the one who would plan to do such a thing?”
He wanted to know who had the heart to make such an evil plan.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵר֔וֹשׁ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לְאֶסְתֵּ֣ר הַמַּלְכָּ֑ה מִ֣י ה֥וּא זֶה֙ וְאֵֽי־ זֶ֣ה ה֔וּא אֲשֶׁר־ מְלָא֥וֹ לִבּ֖וֹ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת כֵּֽן׃

passages.text: Esther replied, “The adversary and enemy is this wicked man—Haman!” And Haman stood in terror before the king and queen.
passages.sermon:
Esther spoke.
She identified the adversary and enemy.
She said, “This wicked man is Haman.”
Haman stood before the king and queen.
Haman was terrified.
passages.original: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר־ אֶסְתֵּ֔ר אִ֚ישׁ צַ֣ר וְאוֹיֵ֔ב הָמָ֥ן הָרָ֖ע הַזֶּ֑ה וְהָמָ֣ן נִבְעַ֔ת מִלִּפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְהַמַּלְכָּֽה׃

passages.text: In his fury, the king arose from drinking his wine and went to the palace garden, while Haman stayed behind to beg Queen Esther for his life, for he realized that the king was planning a terrible fate for him.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes became furious.
He was drinking wine at a banquet.
He stood up in anger.
He left the banquet.
He went to the palace garden.
Haman stayed behind in the room.
Haman begged Queen Esther for his life.
Haman knew the king planned a terrible fate for him.
Haman saw that disaster would come to him from the king.
passages.original: וְהַמֶּ֜לֶךְ קָ֤ם בַּחֲמָתוֹ֙ מִמִּשְׁתֵּ֣ה הַיַּ֔יִן אֶל־ גִּנַּ֖ת הַבִּיתָ֑ן וְהָמָ֣ן עָמַ֗ד לְבַקֵּ֤שׁ עַל־ נַפְשׁוֹ֙ מֵֽאֶסְתֵּ֣ר הַמַּלְכָּ֔ה כִּ֣י רָאָ֔ה כִּֽי־ כָלְתָ֥ה אֵלָ֛יו הָרָעָ֖ה מֵאֵ֥ת הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: Just as the king returned from the palace garden to the banquet hall, Haman was falling on the couch where Esther was reclining. The king exclaimed, “Would he actually assault the queen while I am in the palace?” As soon as the words had left the king’s mouth, they covered Haman’s face.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes was the ruler of Persia.
Queen Esther was his wife.
Haman was an enemy of the Jews.
The king returned from the palace garden.
He entered the banquet hall.
Esther was on a couch.
Haman fell onto the couch where Esther was.
The king saw this.
The king said, “Would Haman attack the queen while I am in the house?”
The king spoke these words.
Immediately, they covered Haman’s face.
passages.original: וְהַמֶּ֡לֶךְ שָׁב֩ מִגִּנַּ֨ת הַבִּיתָ֜ן אֶל־ בֵּ֣ית׀ מִשְׁתֵּ֣ה הַיַּ֗יִן וְהָמָן֙ נֹפֵ֔ל עַל־ הַמִּטָּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶסְתֵּ֣ר עָלֶ֔יהָ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הֲ֠גַם לִכְבּ֧וֹשׁ אֶת־ הַמַּלְכָּ֛ה עִמִּ֖י בַּבָּ֑יִת הַדָּבָ֗ר יָצָא֙ מִפִּ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וּפְנֵ֥י הָמָ֖ן חָפֽוּ׃ס

passages.text: Then Harbonah, one of the eunuchs attending the king, said: “There is a gallows fifty cubits high at Haman’s house. He had it built for Mordecai, who gave the report that saved the king.” “Hang him on it!” declared the king.
passages.sermon:
Harbonah was one of the king’s eunuchs.
Harbonah spoke to the king.
Harbonah said, “There is a gallows at Haman’s house.”
The gallows is fifty cubits high.
Haman built this gallows for Mordecai.
Mordecai had spoken good things about the king.
The king said, “Hang Haman on that gallows.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר חַ֠רְבוֹנָה אֶחָ֨ד מִן־ הַסָּרִיסִ֜ים לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ גַּ֣ם הִנֵּה־ הָעֵ֣ץ אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֪ה הָמָ֟ן לְֽמָרְדֳּכַ֞י אֲשֶׁ֧ר דִּבֶּר־ ט֣וֹב עַל־ הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ עֹמֵד֙ בְּבֵ֣ית הָמָ֔ן גָּבֹ֖הַּ חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים אַמָּ֑ה וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ תְּלֻ֥הוּ עָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: So they hanged Haman on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai. Then the fury of the king subsided.
passages.sermon:
Haman was an enemy of the Jews.
Haman built a gallows for Mordecai.
The king ordered Haman to be hanged.
They hanged Haman on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai.
The king’s anger ended.
passages.original: וַיִּתְלוּ֙ אֶת־ הָמָ֔ן עַל־ הָעֵ֖ץ אֲשֶׁר־ הֵכִ֣ין לְמָרְדֳּכָ֑י וַחֲמַ֥ת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ שָׁכָֽכָה׃פ
